title: Isolate batcher I/O adapters, migrate KV prefetch to epoched adapter, and upgrade libaio
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The continuous batcher and KV prefetch code paths share a number of tightly-coupled I/O and allocator abstractions which have produced intermittent tail-latency spikes under multimodal workloads. Historical hacks (global io threadpool, blocking libaio wrappers) made it fast to ship features but increased maintenance burden, caused subtle memory pressure, and complicated kernel-selection for small/large seq lengths.

Goal: 1) Introduce a pluggable, epoched prefetch adapter that isolates prefetching responsibilities from the batcher commit path and uses leaseless epochs for correctness; 2) Replace the legacy blocking libaio bridge with libaio v2 bindings to reduce syscall overhead and pagefault churn; 3) Slim the scheduler API surface so batcher can opt into non-blocking I/O adapters without pulling the full KV ownership contract.

Success criteria (measurable):
- P95 token latency for 512-token sequences decreases by >= 12% on p100-stable-ec2 workload when prefetch is enabled.
- End-to-end variance (stdev) for 99th percentile requests reduces by >= 20%.
- KV prefetch miss-to-hit stabilization: cold-miss tail drops by >= 30% in synthetic mixed workload.
- No increase in request error rate or memory OOMs in canary for 48h.

Design summary:
- Add adapter interface: PrefetchAdapter { start_epoch(epoch_id), prefetch(keys), drain(epoch_id), metrics() } implemented by: LegacySyncAdapter and EpochedAsyncAdapter.
- EpochedAsyncAdapter uses a small in-process ring + libaiov2 pollset to issue grouped reads; responses are correlated with epoch ids to avoid inter-epoch races.
- Batcher exposes a lightweight prefetch hook (BatcherPrefetchHandle) rather than owning prefetch lifecycle. Scheduler reduced to admit/dismiss + attach-prefetch-handle API.
- Runtime flag: runtime.prefetch.adapter=epoched|legacy; can be toggled per-deployment for rollout.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Adding epoch ids increases bookkeeping but simplifies correctness across retries and rollbacks; we accepted small allocation overhead in exchange for removing complex global locks.
- Upgrading to libaiov2 requires bumping native bindings; this introduces a small dependency window but reduces syscall latency and enables efficient scatter-gather which benefits large-key prefetch.
- We do not convert all IO paths at once; selected path first (kv-prefetch) to limit blast radius.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for adapter interface and epoch correlation.
- Integration tests: synthetic KV hotspot workloads with randomized sequence lengths.
- Soak test: 72h canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic routed to epoched adapter; observe telemetry and heap profiles.
- Perf benchmark harness: compare legacy vs epoched under identical admission profiles (script: infra/bench/prefetch/compare_epoched.sh).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch + CI (PR #1428) with libaio v2 native build.
2) Internal canary on staging (1 node) for correctness.
3) 10% canary in production us-west-2 for 48h.
4) Expand to 50% and run 7-day soak.
5) Full rollout if metrics remain within thresholds.

Fallbacks and mitigations:
- runtime.prefetch.adapter=legacy to disable epoched adapter instantly.
- Automated rollback if P95 increases > 10% or OOM events spike.
- Emergency patch: revert libaio binding change to restore previous IO path binary.

Operational and observability changes:
- New metrics: prefetch.epoch.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, prefetch.epoch.misses, prefetch.adapter.swap_count.
- Tracing span: prefetch:epoch_id attached to request traces for postmortem.
- Dashboards: add prefetched hit-rate tile to Console KVCACHE page and scheduler heatmap for IO wait.

Security: no customer data leaves process boundaries; adapter changes are purely runtime-local. No secrets required.

Docs & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/epoched-prefetch-adapter
- Perf comparison script: infra/bench/prefetch/compare_epoched.sh
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
comments: 2025-02-17 - Maya Chen: Drafted initial design and benchmark plan. Uploaded design doc to Confluence. Noted potential ABI issues with libaio bindings on older centos images.

2025-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Spike completed—prototype epoched adapter shows ~10% reduction in p95 on local bench for 256/512 seq. Native binding build for libaiov2 succeeded on Ubuntu 22.04, failed on centos7 (missing glibc symbols). Added platform gating to CI.

2025-03-01 - Priya Nambiar (review): Reviewed adapter interface. Asked for clearer ownership of inflight epoch state and GC policy. Suggested adding a short TTL-based liveness check to avoid dangling epochs.
2025-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented epoch TTL and added a metrics counter for stale-epoch-reclaims. Bench run with synthetic hotspot workload attached to PR results (see PR #1428).
2025-03-05 - SRE: Approved canary run in us-west-2 pending addition of two alerts: prefetch.adapter.swap_count > 0.1/min and prefetch.epoch.misses spike > 3x baseline.
